sections.theory:
6.3.9 Confidence interval estimate for population proportion p (large sample case)

When the sample size is large the sample proportion \hat{p} has the sampling distribution which is approximately normal with mean p and S.E=\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}} i.e.

$Z=\frac{\hat{p}-p}{\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}}\sim N(0,1)\ \text{as}\ n\to\infty$

A 100(1−α)% confidence interval for p is written as;

$\hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}$

If p is unknown then the confidence interval for p is computed by \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}}

Example 6.16

A random sample of 200 persons from a city was interviewed and 50 of them were found to be literate. Calculate a 90% confidence interval for the proportion of literate persons in the city.

Solution:

A 100 (1−α)% confidence interval for p (literate persons) is \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}}

Given

n = 200, X = 50 (Number of literate persons), therefore \hat{p}=\frac{X}{n}=\frac{50}{200}=0.25, \hat{q}=1-\hat{p}=1-0.25=0.75,

1-\alpha=0.90, \alpha=0.10. From area table of standard normal distribution, we have Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{\frac{0.10}{2}}=Z_{0.05}=1.645

Hence the 90% confidence interval for p is 0.25\pm 1.645\sqrt{\frac{(0.25)(0.75)}{200}}

$\text{or } 0.25\pm 0.05\quad\text{or } (0.2,\ 0.3)\quad\text{or } (0.2<p<0.3)$

6.3.10 Large sample confidence interval estimate for the difference between two population proportions (p₁ − p₂)

A simple extension of the estimation of a binomial proportion p is the estimation of the difference between two binomial proportions. For sufficiently large sample sizes the sampling distribution of \hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2 can be approximated by a normal distribution i.e.

$Z=\frac{(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)-(p_1-p_2)}{\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}}\sim N(0,1)$

The approximate 100(1−α)% confidence interval for (p_1-p_2) is given by:

$(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}$
sections.urdu:
6.3.9 آبادی کے تناسب p کا اعتماد کا وقفہ (بڑے نمونے کی صورت)

جب نمونے کا سائز بڑا ہو تو نمونے کے تناسب \hat{p} کی نمونہ جاتی تقسیم تقریباً نارمل ہوتی ہے جس کا اوسط p اور S.E=\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}} ہے یعنی

$Z=\frac{\hat{p}-p}{\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}}\sim N(0,1)\ \text{as}\ n\to\infty$

p کے لیے 100(1−α)% اعتماد کا وقفہ یوں لکھا جاتا ہے؛

$\hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}$

اگر p نامعلوم ہو تو p کا اعتماد کا وقفہ \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}} سے معلوم کیا جاتا ہے

مثال 6.16

ایک شہر سے 200 افراد کے تصادفی نمونے کا انٹرویو کیا گیا اور ان میں سے 50 خواندہ پائے گئے۔ شہر میں خواندہ افراد کے تناسب کے لیے 90% اعتماد کا وقفہ معلوم کریں۔

حل:

p (خواندہ افراد) کے لیے 100 (1−α)% اعتماد کا وقفہ \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}} ہے

دیا گیا

n = 200، X = 50 (خواندہ افراد کی تعداد)، لہٰذا \hat{p}=\frac{X}{n}=\frac{50}{200}=0.25، \hat{q}=1-\hat{p}=1-0.25=0.75،

1-\alpha=0.90، \alpha=0.10۔ معیاری نارمل تقسیم کے رقبے کے جدول سے ہمارے پاس Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{\frac{0.10}{2}}=Z_{0.05}=1.645 ہے

لہٰذا p کے لیے 90% اعتماد کا وقفہ 0.25\pm 1.645\sqrt{\frac{(0.25)(0.75)}{200}} ہے

$\text{or } 0.25\pm 0.05\quad\text{or } (0.2,\ 0.3)\quad\text{or } (0.2<p<0.3)$

6.3.10 دو آبادیوں کے تناسبوں کے فرق (p₁ − p₂) کا بڑے نمونے کا اعتماد کا وقفہ

دو رقمی تناسب p کے تخمین کی ایک سادہ توسیع دو دو رقمی تناسبوں کے فرق کا تخمین ہے۔ کافی بڑے نمونوں کے لیے \hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2 کی نمونہ جاتی تقسیم کو نارمل تقسیم سے تقریباً ظاہر کیا جا سکتا ہے یعنی

$Z=\frac{(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)-(p_1-p_2)}{\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}}\sim N(0,1)$

(p_1-p_2) کے لیے تقریبی 100(1−α)% اعتماد کا وقفہ یہ ہے:

$(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}$

6.3.10 د دوو نفوسونو د تناسبونو د توپیر (p₁ − p₂) لپاره د لویې نمونې د باور واټن اټکل

6.3.9 Confidence interval estimate for population proportion p (large sample case)

When the sample size is large the sample proportion \hat{p} has the sampling distribution which is approximately normal with mean p and S.E=\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}} i.e.

$Z=\frac{\hat{p}-p}{\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}}\sim N(0,1)\ \text{as}\ n\to\infty$

A 100(1−α)% confidence interval for p is written as;

$\hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{pq}{n}}$

If p is unknown then the confidence interval for p is computed by \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}}

Example 6.16

A random sample of 200 persons from a city was interviewed and 50 of them were found to be literate. Calculate a 90% confidence interval for the proportion of literate persons in the city.

Solution:

A 100 (1−α)% confidence interval for p (literate persons) is \hat{p}\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}\hat{q}}{n}}

Given

n = 200, X = 50 (Number of literate persons), therefore \hat{p}=\frac{X}{n}=\frac{50}{200}=0.25, \hat{q}=1-\hat{p}=1-0.25=0.75,

1-\alpha=0.90, \alpha=0.10. From area table of standard normal distribution, we have Z_{\alpha/2}=Z_{\frac{0.10}{2}}=Z_{0.05}=1.645

Hence the 90% confidence interval for p is 0.25\pm 1.645\sqrt{\frac{(0.25)(0.75)}{200}}

$\text{or } 0.25\pm 0.05\quad\text{or } (0.2,\ 0.3)\quad\text{or } (0.2<p<0.3)$

6.3.10 Large sample confidence interval estimate for the difference between two population proportions (p₁ − p₂)

A simple extension of the estimation of a binomial proportion p is the estimation of the difference between two binomial proportions. For sufficiently large sample sizes the sampling distribution of \hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2 can be approximated by a normal distribution i.e.

$Z=\frac{(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)-(p_1-p_2)}{\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}}\sim N(0,1)$

The approximate 100(1−α)% confidence interval for (p_1-p_2) is given by:

$(\hat{p}_1-\hat{p}_2)\pm Z_{\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1\hat{q}_1}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2\hat{q}_2}{n_2}}$
